..
Issued at 352 PM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

Regional RAP surface analysis through the day shows a 1002 mb low 
entering Minnesota from Nebraska, and GOES imagery shows cloud cover 
overspreading much of the UP. Radar has shown sporadic cells over 
Lake Superior transiting eastward; MRMS indicates light 
accumulations so far today, mostly occuring over Isle Royale, the 
Keweenaw,and Lake Superior. Most amounts are less than 0.2 inches 
but some isolated spots have received up to 0.35 inches. Fog and 
mist beneath low ceilings are common today, particularly in 
northeast flow upslope areas. Temperatures have turned toward 
seasonable; the Keweenaw remains stubbornly in the 40s, while 
southern Menominee County has reached the 70s, and elsewhere falls 
somewhere between the two. 

The rain thus far today comes courtesy of a plume of moisture with 
nearly zonal motion along the US-Canada border, which has descended 
slowly south while navigating around the southern edge of a Hudson 
Bay High. Tonight, further precipitation is anticipated along with 
better forcing and higher accumulations as the Minnesota low 
transits toward and then south of the UP. Per the REFS, the 
probabilities of receiving greater than 0.25" through Tuesday 8 AM 
north of a line from Gogebic to southern Schoolcraft County is 100%; 
chances south of this line are much less, decreasing to 15% in 
southern Menominee County. For 0.6", only a few areas in northern 
Marquette and Baraga Counties show 100%, with elsewhere showing less 
and southern Menominee County at 0%. Thunderstorm potential has 
trended up over the past 24 hours, with CAMs in good agreement and 
now showing scattered cells across the UP through the night. With up 
500-700 J/kg of MUCAPE (REFS mean) and 1.3 - 1.5" of PWAT available 
to work with overnight, some areas may see higher accumulations as 
stronger cells develop.

Lows tonight remain anomalously high in the 40s north and 50s south, 
as northeast winds work through previously advected warm air in 
southern Ontario. This transitions into a brief WAA regime late 
tonight as the Minnesota low approaches from the east, reinforcing 
above-normal lows tonight. Temps return to normal as this low wraps 
in cooler air on its backside through Tuesday, leaving temperatures 
in the 50s for most of the UP, though the southern UP may hit the 
upper 60s. Overcast or nearly overcast skies dominate for the next 
few days.

With several large, ongoing wildfires and suppression efforts under 
way, an Air Quality Alert is in effect today for Baraga, Marquette, 
Iron, Dickinson, and Menominee Counties. Localized pollutant levels 
in those areas may reach Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups with 
potential for Unhealthy. Note that in areas of fog, such as upslope 
areas of Marquette and Baraga Counties, it may be difficult to 
distinguish smoke from fog while driving or outdoors. Sensors may 
not pick up on air quality reductions due to localized nature of 
smoke plumes.

After tonight's precipitation, dry conditions should once again be 
the norm for a few days as high pressure builds in Wednesday into 
Thursday. A much colder airmass is projected to arrive Friday as an 
Alberta clipper digs into the Great Lakes region. At this time, both 
the GFS and Euro show remarkable agreement that this clipper will 
phase with a Colorado low swinging north right around 12Z over the 
lower Great Lakes, generating a steep pressure gradient with 
northerly flow over Lake Superior. Multiple ensembles hint at 
strongly elevated wind potential during Friday. While the jury's 
still out on whether or not this pattern will generate storm-force 
winds over Lake Superior (less over land, but likely still 
elevated), the ECMWF, Canadian, and GFS ensembles agree that 
some form of elevated sustained winds, possibly up to gale-
force, may occur. Soundings show a cold airmass well below 0C 
being advected in with deep mixing, reinforcing this notion. 
Details of this event will continue to evolve.
